chunks: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Bukayr from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A man asked him about two sisters and a husband, so he said, 'Half and half.' The man said, 'May Allah improve you, has Allah specified for them more than this? For them is the two-thirds.' He said, 'What do you say about a brother and a husband?' He said, 'Half and half.' He said, 'Has not Allah specified for him the entire wealth?' He said, 'And he inherits it if she has no child.'
ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a husband and two sisters when there are no children?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the inheritance distribution between a husband and two sisters by employing a logical analogy with the share of a husband and a single brother. The Imam demonstrates that since the Quran explicitly assigns the husband half the estate when there are no descendants, this fixed portion remains constant regardless of whether the remaining half is divided among sisters or a brother, thereby refuting the questioner's assumption of variable shares. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the immutability of the *fara'id* (fixed shares) derived directly from the Quranic text.
